mn7:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn7:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn7:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, suppose a cloth were defiled and stained,
mn7:2.2: and a dyer dipped it in some dye or other, whether blue or yellow or red or pink, it would look ill-dyed and impure in colour.
mn7:2.4: Because of the impurity of the cloth;
mn7:2.5: so too, when mind is defiled, an unhappy destination may be expected.
mn7:2.6: ‘Bhikkhus, suppose a cloth were pure and bright,
mn7:2.7: and a dyer dipped it in some dye or other, whether blue or yellow or red or pink, it would look well-dyed and pure in colour.
mn7:2.9: Because of the purity of the cloth;
mn7:2.10: so too, when mind is undefiled, a happy destination may be expected.
mn7:3.1: ‘What are the imperfections that defile mind?
mn7:3.2: Covetousness and unrighteous greed is an imperfection that defile mind. Ill-will … Anger … Revenge … Contempt … Domineering … Envy … Avarice … Deceit … Fraud … Obduracy … Presumption … Conceit … Pride (haughtiness) … Vanity … Negligence … is an imperfection that defile mind.
mn7:4.1: ‘When a bhikkhu knows that covetousness and unrighteous greed is an imperfection that defile mind, he abandons it.
mn7:4.30: negligence are imperfections that defile mind,
mn7:5.1: ‘As soon as it is known that covetousness and unrighteous greed is an imperfection that defiles mind, it is abandoned in him;
mn7:5.2: as soon as it is known that ill-will
mn7:5.31: negligence are imperfections that defile mind, they are abandoned in him.
mn7:5.32: ‘Thereupon, he becomes possessed of perfect confidence in the Buddha thus:
mn7:5.33:
“That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant, fully enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds,’

incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.”
mn7:6.1: ‘And he becomes possessed of confidence in the Dhamma thus:
mn7:6.2: “The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, (it has effect) visible here and now, not (after a lapse) of time; it invites inspection, is onward-leading, and experienceable by the wise each for himself.”
mn7:7.1: ‘And he becomes possessed of perfect confidence in the Sangha thus:
mn7:7.2: “The Sangha of the Blessed One’s disciples has entered on the good way, has entered on the straight way, has entered on the true way, has entered on the proper way, that is to say, the four Pairs of Men, the Eight (types of) Persons; this Sangha of the Blessed One’s disciples is fit for gifts, fit for hospitality, fit for offerings, and fit for reverential salutation, as the incomparable field of merit for the world.”
mn7:8.1:
‘And whatever (from among those imperfections) has, according to the limitation (set by whichever of the first three paths he has attained), been given up, has been (for ever) dropped, let go, abandoned, relinquished.

‘He (considers) thus: “I am possessed of perfect confidence in the Buddha” and he gains experience of meanings, he gains experience of dhammas, and so he finds gladness connected with the Dhamma.
mn7:8.2: ‘When he is glad, happiness is born in him; being happy in mind, his body becomes tranquillized; when his body is tranquil, he feels pleasure; feeling pleasure, his mind becomes concentrated.
mn7:9.1: ‘He (considers) thus: “I am possessed of perfect confidence in the Dhamma” and he gains experience of meanings, he gains experience of dhammas, and so he finds gladness connected with the Dhamma.
mn7:10.1: ‘He (considers) thus: “I am possessed of perfect confidence in the Sangha” and he gains experience of meanings, he gains experience of dhammas, and so he finds gladness connected with the Dhamma.
mn7:10.2: ‘When he is glad … his mind becomes concentrated.
mn7:11.1: ‘He (considers) thus: “And whatever has, according to limitation, been given up, it has been dropped, let go, abandoned, relinquished, and he gains experience of meanings, he gains experience of dhammas, and so he finds gladness connected with the Dhamma.
mn7:11.2: ‘When he is glad … his mind becomes concentrated.
mn7:12.1: ‘If a bhikkhu of such virtue, such dhammas and such understanding eats alms-food consisting of rice with the dark grains picked out accompanied by many sauces and curries, even that will be no obstacle for him.
mn7:12.2: ‘Just as a cloth that is defiled and stained becomes pure and bright with the help of clear water, or just as gold becomes pure and bright with the help of a furnace,
mn7:12.3: so too, if a bhikkhu of such virtue … eats alms-food … that will be no obstacle for him.
mn7:13.1: ‘He abides with his heart endued with loving-kindness extending over one quarter, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth, and so above, below, around and everywhere, and to all as to himself; he abides with his heart abundant with loving-kindness, exalted, measureless, without hostility or ill-will extending over the all-encompassing world.
mn7:14.1: ‘He abides with his heart endued with compassion … over the all-encompassing world.
mn7:15.1: ‘He abides with his heart endued with gladness … over the all-encompassing world.
mn7:16.1: ‘He abides with his heart endued with equanimity … over the all-encompassing world.
mn7:17.1: ‘(Of that) he understands thus: “There is this (pure state of Divine Abiding), there is the inferior (state of defilements abandoned), there is the superior (goal of the Arahant Path yet to be attained), and there is the escape (which is Nibbāna) from this (whole) field of perception.”
mn7:18.1: ‘When he knows and sees in this way, the mind becomes liberated from the taint of sensual desire, liberated from the taint of being, and liberated from the taint of ignorance.
mn7:18.2: When liberated, there is knowledge: “It is liberated”.
mn7:18.3: He understands: “Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what can be done is done, there is no more of this in the beyond.”
mn7:19.1: Now on that occasion Sundavika Bhāradvāja of the divine caste had seated himself not far from the Blessed One.
mn7:19.2: Then he said to the Blessed One:
mn7:19.3: ‘But does Master Gotama go to the Bahukā River to bathe?’
mn7:19.5: What can the Bahukā River do?’
mn7:19.6: ‘Master Gotama, the Bahukā River is held by many to give liberation; it is held by many to give merit, and many wash away in the Bahukā River the evil kammas they have done.’
mn7:20.1: Then the Blessed One addressed Sundarika Bhāradvāja of the divine caste in stanzas:
mn7:20.7: Yet will not wash black kamma white.
mn7:20.8: What can Sundarikā bring to pass?
mn7:20.9: What the Payāga? What the Bahukā?
mn7:20.11: A man that has done brutal acts and cruel.
mn7:20.12: One pure in heart has evermore
mn7:20.13: The Feast of Spring, the Holy Day;
mn7:20.14: One fair in act, one pure in heart
mn7:20.16: ’Tis here, divine, that thou shouldst come to bathe,
mn7:20.17: To make thyself safe refuge for all beings.
mn7:20.18: And if thou speakest no untruth,
mn7:20.19: Nor workest harm for living beings,
mn7:20.20: Nor takest what is offered not,
mn7:20.21: With faith and with no avarice,
mn7:20.22: To Gayā gone what wouldst thou do?
mn7:20.23: Let any well thy Gayā be.
mn7:21.1: When this was said, Sundarika Bhāradvāja of the divine caste said:
mn7:21.3: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who is lost, holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms.
mn7:21.4: ‘I go to Master Gotama for refuge and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha.
mn7:21.5: I would receive the Going-forth under Master Gotama, I would receive the Full Admission.’
mn7:22.1: And Sundarika Bhāradvāja of the divine caste received the Going-forth under the Blessed One, and he received the Full Admission.
mn7:22.2: And not long after his Full Admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent and self-controlled, the venerable Bhāradvāja, by realization himself with direct knowledge here and now, entered upon and abode in that supreme goal of the life divine, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn7:22.3: He had direct knowledge thus: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived, what is to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’
mn7:22.4: And the venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the Arahants.
